title: St. Mary's Italian band and buying his first trombone
summary: He and Tony Parenti played in an Italian band; he started on another horn, was steered to trombone, got lessons and a nine-dollar horn, and a neighbour heard him practicing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Did you know Tony Perrini when you were a kid?

Oh sure, we went to school together and we started together. We played an Italian band at St. Mary's Church, you know? Oh yeah. They had an Italian band that used to rehearse in the backyard, had a big room there. In fact, when I first started there I played peclone I see, instead of trombone. I didn't like it. It didn't mean nothing. I couldn't, I mean there was no sense. You couldn't play, you played melody, you would just plump, plump, plump, you know?

One of those things. So, my father said, you know they need trombone players. Trombones were scarce. That was the truth. They didn't have many trombones at that time. So, this fellow used to pass my house all the time. My dad knew him. And he said, why don't you teach that boy how to play an instrument. So, he asked me, what would I like to play? I said, trumpet. He said, well you know they need trombone players, why don't you? I'm going to take lessons on trombone. He said, I can give you some lessons. So, he gave me some lessons and all that stuff. So, I got tired. I said, you know, so phasian, I didn't have a horn yet. I said, look, I've been so phasian, you know, that's reading music, timing and all that stuff. I said, I'm getting tired of this. I said, I don't get a horn. I said, let's just forget about it. So, he told my dad, he went up there and he said, you know something? If you don't give that boy a horn, he's going to quit. He's going to forget about it. So, the next day he says, okay, go ahead and buy him a horn. So, the horn cost nine hours. At that time the horn was cheap. I mean, for eighteen, nineteen or something like that. Bought it for nine hours. And I started playing on it for good horn. And then I started practicing in New York. And would you believe, Vic, that I got offered a co-player of the band? While you were practicing? Practicing. I just bought the horn. See, I was in New York and started practicing. So, the guy knocked on the door. My mother went to the door. And the father said, I speak to that trombone player. She said, well, they're Italian people. Well, that's my son. I said, well, can I talk to him? She said, yeah. So, she called me. So, this father says, was that you playing trombone back there? I said, yeah, I just bought the horn. I said, I'm practicing. I get something out of it. He said, well, who is playing besides you? I said, no, I didn't play myself. I'm practicing. He said, you mean you just bought a horn and you blow a horn like that? I said, I don't know. I just, you know, got the idea. Well, he told me what to do, you know, how to blow it and all that stuff. So, would you believe I went to work for ballet, like the fight, the playlist house and all that stuff, and Dan Hughes, you know?
